grain: One row per (ip_right_type, application_number, party_id, party_role_category, party_role, effective_from_date) party-role episode on a single IP application; the same party_id can appear on many applications and the same application can carry several parties and roles, so no single column is a key. Rows are a prefix cohort of 25,000 records, not the full party_activity.csv.

groups.name: ip_application_identity
groups.purpose: Identifies the IP application the party-role episode attaches to. ip_right_type scopes application_number, so the pair is the application identifier; neither column alone is a key.

groups.name: party_identity
groups.purpose: Identifies the party (organisation or individual) involved in the application. party_id is a party identifier, not a company registration number; abn is sparsely populated and must not be used to infer legal form; party_name is free text and not a join key.

groups.name: party_role_on_application
groups.purpose: The role the party plays on this application. party_role_category and party_role are distinct dimensions; applicant, patentee and agent roles must not be collapsed, and an agent row is not evidence of ownership.

groups.name: party_address
groups.purpose: Party address fields as supplied. Mixed formats (post_code holds values like 't6b 3n9' and '110044'); not normalised, and country_code is not a statement of the party's legal jurisdiction.

groups.name: party_activity_validity
groups.purpose: Validity of the party-role episode and party attribute flags. Dates are party-activity validity dates, not company incorporation or IP right grant/expiry dates; is_current refers to the party record, not enforceability of the right; is_founding is a supplied flag, not evidence of incorporation.

entity_types.name: ip_application
entity_types.definition: An IP application identified by the pair (ip_right_type, application_number); the right type scopes the application number.

entity_types.name: party
entity_types.definition: An organisation or individual recorded as a party on an IP application, identified by party_id; party_type distinguishes organisation from individual. Not a statement of legal form or company status.

ip_application.rationale: application_number is scoped by ip_right_type, so the pair is the application identifier; the same numeric string could occur under different right types.

party.rationale: party_id is the party identifier; abn is sparse and party_name is free text, so neither is a key and neither supports legal-form inference.

relationship_types.name: PARTY_INVOLVED_IN_APPLICATION
relationship_types.definition: A party is recorded on an IP application in a specific party role (applicant, patentee, agent or other), for a party-activity validity period.

relationships.rationale: Each row pairs a party_id with an (ip_right_type, application_number) application and a party_role/party_role_category; the role and effective dates qualify the involvement rather than changing the entities.

cautions: party_id is a party identifier, not a company registration number; abn is sparsely populated and must not be used to infer legal company status or legal form.
party_name is free text, lower-cased and unnormalised; names are not unique identifiers and should not be used to join or deduplicate parties.

party_type (organisation/individual) and party_role_category/party_role (applicant, patentee, agent) are distinct dimensions; applicant, patentee and agent roles must not be collapsed, and an agent row is not evidence of ownership.
application_number is an IP application identifier scoped by ip_right_type; treat the pair as the identifier.

effective_from_date / effective_to_date are party-activity validity dates, not company incorporation dates and not IP right grant or expiry dates; is_current refers to the party record, not to enforceability of the right.
is_founding is a party attribute flag as supplied; it is not evidence of company incorporation and should not be read as a legal founding date.
state_code, post_code and country_code are party address fields with mixed formats; they are not normalised and country_code is not a statement of the party's legal jurisdiction.
The cohort is prefix-biased (first 25,000 CSV records, no filtering); no population-level or full-archive claims can be made.
No joins to application status, descriptions or classifications are available in this source; a current party activity is not evidence the IP right is currently enforceable.
